description: We are Voyager 3, a team of 5 Grade 11 students from STEM Sharkia School, united by a deep curiosity for science and space exploration. Driven by a passion for innovation and critical thinking, we view the NASA Space Apps Challenge as the ultimate opportunity to apply our scientific knowledge, explore the mysteries of the universe, and translate space data into meaningful, real-world solutions.
summary:
Moon Mission is an educational lunar survival game with 7 stages powered by real NASA open data. Players become astronauts tasked with building base stations and managing vital resources to survive the dangers of real space and establish a permanent base on the Moon.
​Our project tackles the challenge by turning complex scientific datasets into interactive gameplay mechanics instead of invented numbers. Players protect from real solar flares with DONKI space weather data, manage greenhouses with OSDR space biology research, protect from cosmic rays with RadLab radiation measurements, and scan craters for water ice with Mars Trek terrain maps.
This project is important because it makes space science accessible and engaging for children through “stealth learning”, inspiring future STEM explorers while unlocking real NASA APOD imagery as a reward. This game also helps build children's characters and early passions by forcing them to face the consequences based on what they choose as the solution for the challenges that they face throughout the stages. Eventually, this game will have a role in introducing problem solving skills, resource management, prioritization, and long term planning from an early stage in their lives.
details:
Moon Mission is an interactive 7-stage educational space survival game for children. Instead of relying on fictional game mechanics, players are cast in the role of an astronaut who must build and maintain a lunar outpost, using real NASA open datasets:

DONKI (Space Weather): Simulates real-time solar flares and geomagnetic storms that players actively defend their base against.

OSDR (Space Biology): Provides guidance for management of resources, oxygen production and growing of crops in lunar greenhouses.

RadLab (Radiation): Players must monitor levels of cosmic radiation and upgrade base shielding as needed.

Mars Trek & Planetary Terrain Data: For crater analysis, rugged terrain navigation and water ice deposit scanning.

APOD (Astronomy Picture of the Day): Gives children a reward of actual photography from NASA spacecraft upon completion of stages.

Benefits & Intended Impact

The project bridges the gap between complex scientific telemetry and accessible, engaging gameplay through "stealth learning." It empowers children to develop critical thinking, resource management, and problem-solving skills while inspiring the next generation of STEM explorers to engage with real world NASA missions.

​Tools & Technologies Used

​Frontend & Game Logic: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (built as a lightweight, browser-accessible web application).

​Data Architecture: Hybrid architecture combining live NASA Open API fetching with an embedded local dataset to guarantee 100% offline stability during live demonstrations.

​Design & Presentation: Canva for visual assets and pitch deck design.

​Creativity & Considerations

Our team focused on a System-of-Systems Design, integrating 5 distinct NASA datasets into one cohesive survival loop rather than relying on a single data feed. We prioritized accessibility, offline reliability, and replacing generic virtual coins with real NASA imagery so every reward teaches kids something real about our universe.
